content: Per-language name/version/description extraction chains (cross-checked across snyk, langforge, repo-scanner, detect-stack, Understand-Anything): Name priority = manifest name field, then module/package path segment (go.mod module last segment; composer vendor/package; pom artifactId; PackageId/AssemblyName in .csproj; rootProject.name in settings.gradle), then folder name. Version is OPTIONAL or derived in most ecosystems: pyproject.toml version is often dynamic = ["version"] (PEP 621: name required, version required-or-dynamic, description optional); composer.json version should be OMITTED when VCS tags exist (Packagist derives from tags; hardcoded version conflicts); pom.xml version frequently inherited from parent; build.gradle version lives in Groovy/Kotlin code (not declaratively readable); .csproj Version defaults to 1.0.0 when absent (cannot distinguish intended from default statically); package.json version optional in practice (private packages omit); go.mod has NO project version - the go directive is a toolchain FLOOR (mise docs explicitly treat floor fields as not-version). Description: manifest description optional everywhere and absent in go.mod/gradle; README first paragraph/10-line head fallback is used by Understand-Anything and detect-stack. Best-effort expectation: never error on absence, empty or Unknown result instead; never execute build tools or network calls to resolve dynamic versions.
